title: Heatwaves: When Does Heat Become a Disaster?

endcard.line: Pictures: NASA Solar Dynamics Observatory; Andrew Cattoir, US National Park Service (public domain)

segments.say: Forty degrees in Delhi in May is normal. So when does a hot day become a heatwave? India has a rule for it.

anim.title: IMD: a heatwave needs
items: And well above the normal for that place

segments.say: First, the temperature must cross a floor: forty degrees in the plains, thirty-seven on the coast, thirty in the hills. Then it must be well above normal for that place.
Four and a half to six point four degrees above normal is a heatwave. More than that is a severe heatwave.
And sometimes the number alone is enough. Forty-five degrees is a heatwave anywhere in the plains; forty-seven is severe.
Heat becomes a disaster when bodies can't cool down: outdoor workers, the old, the very young, people without water or shade, and nights that never cool.
So cities now write heat action plans. Ahmedabad made South Asia's first in twenty thirteen. Warnings, water, shade, changed work hours and ready hospitals.
For GS Three: the heat is the hazard; the disaster depends on who is exposed and how ready we are.

sources: IMD, 'Heat Wave' criteria (FAQ, mausam.imd.gov.in): heat wave considered when maximum temperature reaches at least 40°C in plains, 37°C in coastal stations and 30°C in hilly regions; departure from normal 4.5–6.4°C is a heat wave, above 6.4°C severe; or actual maximum ≥45°C heat wave, ≥47°C severe heat wave
NDMA, Guidelines for Preparation of Action Plan – Prevention and Management of Heat Wave (2019): vulnerable groups, heat action plans, early warning, cooling measures
Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation / NRDC, Ahmedabad Heat Action Plan (2013): the first heat action plan in South Asia

quiz.q: What is the minimum temperature for a heatwave in the plains?
quiz.why: IMD's floor for the plains is 40°C, and the day must also be well above normal.

quiz.q: How far above normal makes a severe heatwave?
quiz.why: 4.5 to 6.4°C above normal is a heatwave; more than 6.4°C is severe.

quiz.q: Which city made South Asia's first heat action plan?

reviewNote: Facts were read against IMD's heatwave criteria, NDMA's 2019 guidelines and the Ahmedabad plan. Tone is serious: no deaths counted, no music. Moving facts: IMD may revise its criteria.
